name: safegit
help: concurrency-safe git wrapper providing 31 commands for multi-agent use with atomic commits, oplog-based undo, and history rewriting

global_flags.name: config-file
global_flags.help: path to a custom safegit config file instead of the default location; when omitted the default location is used

commit.name: commit
commit.help: stage and commit specified files in a single atomic operation

flags.name: m
flags.help: commit message line; can be repeated to build multi-line messages

flags.name: F
flags.help: read the full commit message body from a file instead of --m flags

flags.name: branch
flags.help: commit the staged files onto a different branch without switching to it

flags.name: amend
flags.help: amend the current HEAD commit by replacing it with updated content; omitted means a new commit

flags.name: allow-empty
flags.help: allow creating a commit even when no files have been changed; omitted means an empty commit is refused

flags.name: trailer
flags.help: add a key-value trailer line to the commit message (repeatable)

args.name: files
args.help: files to commit (supports hunk specs: file.go:1,3)

grants.name: parent-bump
grants.reason: committing in a submodule moves the parent's gitlink, so safegit commits the parent too when commit.autoBumpParent is on

checkout.name: checkout
checkout.help: checkout a branch or ref with working-tree safety guards

merge.name: merge
merge.help: merge a branch into HEAD with working-tree safety guards

rebase.name: rebase
rebase.help: rebase current branch onto upstream with safety guards

reset.name: reset
reset.help: reset HEAD with guards that prevent accidental --hard data loss

bisect.name: bisect
bisect.help: binary search through commits to find a bug, with safety guards

push.name: push
push.help: push refs to remote with pre-pre-push hooks and automatic retry

flags.name: pre-push-hook
flags.help: run pre-pre-push hook scripts before pushing to remote; omitted means the hooks run

flags.name: force-with-lease
flags.help: force push using --force-with-lease to prevent overwriting others' work; omitted means an ordinary push

flags.name: refs
flags.help: which refs to push

choices.help: push only the current HEAD branch to the remote, ignoring other refs
push all local branches to the remote, ignoring tags and other refs
push all local tags to the remote without pushing any branches
push all local branches and all tags to the remote in one operation

args.name: remote
args.help: name of the remote repository to push to (defaults to origin)

grants.name: push
grants.reason: publishing local refs to a remote is what this command is for

grants.name: force-push
grants.reason: --force-with-lease overwrites the remote ref, discarding whatever the lease expectation did not cover

pull.name: pull
pull.help: fetch from remote and merge, defaulting to fast-forward-only mode

flags.name: merge-strategy
flags.help: how the fetched commits are merged into the current branch

choices.help: fast-forward when possible, otherwise create a merge commit
fast-forward only, refusing the pull when the branches have diverged
always create a merge commit, even when a fast-forward is possible

args.name: remote
args.help: name of the remote repository to pull from (defaults to origin)

args.name: branch
args.help: name of the remote branch to fetch and merge into the current branch

doctor.name: doctor
doctor.help: run diagnostic health checks on the repository and optionally repair issues

flags.name: action
flags.help: what doctor does with the health checks it runs

choices.help: run all health checks and report results without fixing any issues
run all health checks and automatically repair any issues found
remove all safegit hooks and metadata from this repository entirely

cherry-pick.name: cherry-pick
cherry-pick.help: cherry-pick one or more commits onto HEAD with safety guards

revert.name: revert
revert.help: revert one or more commits creating inverse patches, with safety guards

undo.name: undo
undo.help: reverse the last commit, amend, or reword operation using the oplog

flags.name: bypass-session
flags.help: undo across all sessions by ignoring the session ID ownership check; omitted means only this session's operations are undone

flags.name: count
flags.help: number of oplog operations to undo in a single invocation; omitted means one

grants.name: parent-bump
grants.reason: undoing a submodule commit moves the parent's gitlink back, so safegit commits the parent too when commit.autoBumpParent is on

unlock.name: unlock
unlock.help: release a stale .lock file left behind by a crashed git process

args.name: ref
args.help: the ref name (e.g. refs/heads/main) whose stale .lock file to remove

scan.name: scan
scan.help: search git history for regex pattern matches across all objects and working tree files, scanning blobs, commit messages, tag annotations, and trailers with optional scope filtering and commit range selection

flags.name: pattern
flags.help: regular expression pattern to search for across all objects in history

flags.name: scope
flags.help: glob pattern limiting which blob file paths are included (e.g. '*.env', 'config/**')

flags.name: from
flags.help: first commit hash to include when scanning history (mutually exclusive with --entire-history)

flags.name: entire-history
flags.help: scan all commits from the root of the repository to HEAD (mutually exclusive with --from)

flags.name: target
flags.help: comma-separated list of match types to include: blobs,commits,tags,trailers,files (default: all)

version.name: version
version.help: print safegit version, Go runtime version, and git version

backup.name: backup
backup.help: push, list, and restore per-branch history backups held in the tool-owned refs/backups namespace on a remote, so uncommitted-to-the-world work survives a lost machine without ever touching refs/heads

backup.name: backup
backup.help: push the current branch to its backup slot refs/backups/<branch> on the remote, after fetching that slot and refusing when it holds commits your history does not contain; the push is pinned with --force-with-lease to the exact SHA that was just observed (or to "this ref must not exist" for a first backup), so a concurrent backup from another machine is rejected rather than clobbered; plain git equivalent: git push --force-with-lease=refs/backups/<branch>:<observed-sha> <remote> HEAD:refs/backups/<branch>

flags.name: overwrite-remote-backup
flags.help: replace a backup slot whose commits are missing from your current history, leasing on the SHA observed during this run; omitted, and with --no-overwrite-remote-backup, such a slot is a hard error because overwriting it would drop work backed up from elsewhere

flags.name: allow-public-remote
flags.help: consent to backing up to a remote that is public, or whose visibility safegit cannot determine; omitted, and with --no-allow-public-remote, such a target is a question, asked at the terminal and refused outright when there is none, because a backup pushes the whole branch and --approve-consequential says nothing about where

args.name: remote
args.help: name of the remote repository holding the backup slots (defaults to origin)

grants.name: push
grants.reason: a backup slot is only useful once it is on the remote

grants.name: force-push
grants.reason: a backup slot is a single overwritten slot, pinned by a lease to the SHA observed a moment earlier

list.name: list
list.help: list every backup slot present on the remote with the branch name and the commit each slot points at, so you can see which branches are backed up from which machine before restoring one; plain git equivalent: git ls-remote <remote> 'refs/backups/*'

args.name: remote
args.help: name of the remote repository holding the backup slots (defaults to origin)

restore.name: restore
restore.help: fetch the current branch's backup slot from the remote and fast-forward the branch onto it, refusing when the local branch carries commits the backup does not contain so no local work is ever discarded; plain git equivalent: git fetch <remote> refs/backups/<branch> && git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD

args.name: remote
args.help: name of the remote repository holding the backup slots (defaults to origin)

config.name: config
config.help: show, get, or set safegit configuration key-value pairs

show.name: show
show.help: show all configuration values currently in effect for this repository, including built-in defaults and any user overrides from the .git/safegit/config.json file, printed as key-value pairs to stdout for inspection and debugging purposes

get.name: get
get.help: get the current value of a single configuration key from the .git/safegit/config.json file, printing the raw value to stdout so it can be captured by scripts or used in automation pipelines

args.name: key
args.help: the configuration key whose current value should be retrieved

set.name: set
set.help: set a configuration key to a new value in the .git/safegit/config.json file, creating the file if it does not exist yet, and persisting the change for all future safegit invocations in this repository

args.name: key
args.help: the configuration key to set to the specified value in config.json

args.name: value
args.help: the new value to assign to the specified configuration key

hook.name: hook
hook.help: manage pre-pre-push hook scripts that run before every push

list.name: list
list.help: list all pre-pre-push hooks currently installed in the .git/safegit/hooks directory, showing each hook name, file path, and whether it is executable, so you can audit which checks run before every push

run.name: run
run.help: run all installed pre-pre-push hooks (or a single named hook) immediately without performing an actual push, so you can verify that all configured hooks pass before committing to a real push operation
run.dry_run_unsupported_reason: running a hook executes an operator-supplied script whose effects safegit cannot know in advance, so there is nothing honest to preview; run 'safegit hook list' to see which scripts would run

args.name: name
args.help: name of a specific hook to run; omit to run all installed hooks

install.name: install
install.help: install a pre-pre-push hook by copying a script file into the .git/safegit/hooks directory, making it executable, and registering it so that safegit push will run it before any network I/O occurs

args.name: path
args.help: filesystem path to the hook script file to install into safegit

author.name: author
author.help: audit and rewrite commit author/committer identity — list all identities, check against expected values, and rewrite name or email across history

list.name: list
list.help: list all distinct author and committer identities across the entire commit history, showing name, email, role, and commit count for each unique identity — useful for auditing repositories with multiple contributors or detecting unwanted identity variations such as typos, old email addresses, or bot accounts that should be consolidated before a rewrite

check.name: check
check.help: check that all commits use the expected author and committer identity by scanning every commit in the repository history, reporting any deviations with the exact commit hashes and mismatched fields, and suggesting the corresponding safegit author rewrite command to fix each deviation found

flags.name: name
flags.help: expected author and committer display name that all commits should use

flags.name: email
flags.help: expected author and committer email address that all commits should use

rewrite.name: rewrite
rewrite.help: rewrite author and committer name or email across all commit history using git filter-branch style rewriting, replacing every occurrence of the old identity with the new one in both author and committer fields while preserving timestamps, commit messages, tree contents, and parent relationships so the rewritten history is otherwise identical to the original

flags.name: old-name
flags.help: current author or committer display name to search for and replace

flags.name: new-name
flags.help: new display name to substitute wherever the old name is found in history

flags.name: old-email
flags.help: current author or committer email address to search for and replace

flags.name: new-email
flags.help: new email address to substitute wherever the old email is found in history

scrub.name: scrub
scrub.help: surgically rewrite git history to remove or replace sensitive content using 4 subcommands (file, match, run, verify) that operate on all commits, trees, and blobs in the repository

file.name: file
file.help: replace or remove a specific file across all commits in the repository history, rewriting each affected commit tree to either substitute the file contents with a sanitized version or delete the file entirely from every historical snapshot

flags.name: from
flags.help: first commit hash to include when rewriting history

flags.name: reason
flags.help: mandatory audit trail message explaining why this scrub operation is needed

flags.name: remap-shas-in
flags.help: glob selecting files whose full 40-character commit hashes are remapped to the rewritten SHAs during the walk, keeping hash-referencing files like JSONL changelogs self-consistent at every commit (repeatable; same matching semantics as --scope; not applied inside submodule histories)

args.name: file
args.help: repository-relative path to the file that should be scrubbed from history

match.name: match
match.help: replace all occurrences of a regex pattern across every blob in the repository history, rewriting commit trees to substitute matched text with a replacement string so that sensitive values like secrets and credentials are permanently removed from all historical snapshots

flags.name: pattern
flags.help: regular expression pattern to search for across all blobs in history

flags.name: reason
flags.help: mandatory audit trail message explaining why this scrub operation is needed

flags.name: scope
flags.help: glob pattern limiting which file paths are searched (e.g. '*.env', 'config/**')

flags.name: remap-shas-in
flags.help: glob selecting files whose full 40-character commit hashes are remapped to the rewritten SHAs during the walk, keeping hash-referencing files like JSONL changelogs self-consistent at every commit (repeatable; same matching semantics as --scope; not applied inside submodule histories)

flags.name: substitution
flags.help: what replaces each match

choices.name: replace
choices.help: substitute a literal string for every match

flags.name: value
flags.help: literal string to substitute for each regex match found in history

choices.name: mangle
choices.help: substitute random printable ASCII of the same length for every match

flags.name: range
flags.help: how much of the history is rewritten

choices.name: from
choices.help: rewrite the commits from a given commit forward

flags.name: value
flags.help: first commit hash to include when rewriting history

choices.name: entire-history
choices.help: rewrite every commit from the root of the repository to HEAD

run.name: run
run.help: execute a multi-operation scrub recipe from a TOML file, applying all pattern replacements and file removals across history in a single coordinated pass with topological commit ordering, overlap detection between operations, and automatic verification that no matched content survives in the rewritten object store — use --diff to preview all changes as unified diffs before committing to the rewrite

flags.name: reason
flags.help: mandatory audit trail message explaining why this scrub operation is needed

flags.name: diff
flags.help: preview what would change without modifying any objects, showing unified diffs; omitted means the rewrite is performed

flags.name: limit
flags.help: maximum number of blob diffs to show in --diff mode; omitted means 50

flags.name: remap-shas-in
flags.help: glob selecting files whose full 40-character commit hashes are remapped to the rewritten SHAs during the walk, keeping hash-referencing files like JSONL changelogs self-consistent at every commit (repeatable; same matching semantics as --scope; not applied inside submodule histories)

flags.name: range
flags.help: how much of the history is rewritten

choices.name: from
choices.help: rewrite the commits from a given commit forward

flags.name: value
flags.help: first commit hash to include when rewriting history

choices.name: entire-history
choices.help: rewrite every commit from the root of the repository to HEAD

args.name: recipe
args.help: path to the TOML recipe file containing scrub operations

verify.name: verify
verify.help: check all scrub policies defined in the repository configuration to confirm that previously scrubbed secrets and sensitive patterns remain completely absent from every object in the git object store, scanning blobs, commit messages, and tag annotations and reporting detailed per-policy pass or fail results with match locations for any violations found

handshakes.help: Claude Code session identifier set by the invoking agent session; scopes 'safegit undo' to operations this session performed and is recorded as a commit trailer
